Optimal.Notes: A 1024x640 internal render with FSR gives a reasonable balance of image quality and GPU headroom; medium textures and terrain improve readability of the environment without tanking performance. GE-Proton is recommended for the best chance of BattlEye compatibility on community servers.

profiles.Summary: DayZ is a demanding open-world survival game that sits right at the edge of the Steam Deck's GPU capability — the minimum GPU (GTX 760) is below Deck level but the recommended GPU (GTX 1060/RX 580) exceeds it, meaning low-to-medium settings with upscaling are required to reach a stable 30 fps. The game uses BattlEye anti-cheat, which has historically caused Linux compatibility issues, and is listed as Unsupported on Steam Deck, so expect potential connectivity or anti-cheat hurdles.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck or Linux player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements versus Deck GPU capability. On first launch, check frame rate in a populated town — if it drops below 25 fps consistently, drop to the Max Battery profile and reduce Visibility further.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling cuts GPU load significantly; a TDP cap of 8 W and a fixed GPU clock help stabilise power draw. BattlEye compatibility with GE-Proton is generally better than stock Proton, but server access is not guaranteed.

KnownIssues: BattlEye anti-cheat is enabled and may block online play on Linux/Proton — some servers require BattlEye to be active and functional, which is not guaranteed on Deck.
Game is officially 'Unsupported' on Steam Deck; Bohemia Interactive does not provide official Linux support.
No controller layout is officially provided; you will need a community controller layout or custom bindings for the complex keyboard/mouse-heavy UI.
Performance in densely populated towns or with many players nearby can cause significant frame drops even on capable PCs.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Running at full TDP with the GPU at max clock and a 1152x720 render target, medium settings are achievable in open fields, but expect drops into the high 20s in towns or during heavy PvP. Shadows are kept Low as they are the single biggest performance cost in DayZ.

Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz refresh gives the smoothest perceived motion for this survival game; FSR from 1024x640 keeps visuals acceptable while easing GPU load. GE-Proton is recommended by the community to best handle VAC and online connectivity.

profiles.Summary: DayZ runs on the Steam Deck at a gold ProtonDB tier, meaning most players get it working well with some tweaks, though its VAC anti-cheat and online-only nature can cause friction. The game's recommended GPU (GTX 1060 / RX 580) is above the Deck's capability, so low settings with FSR upscaling are necessary to maintain playable frame rates.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck-specific reports or guides were available; profiles are estimated from PC minimum/recommended requirements versus Deck GPU capability (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class) and DayZ's Enfusion/Arma engine behaviour. On first run, check frame rate in a populated town or forest — if it drops below 25 fps consistently, switch to Max Battery settings and lower View Distance further.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 and an 8 W TDP cap gives the longest session life; the 30 fps cap keeps frame pacing smooth and prevents GPU spikes. Note that in-game option names are estimated from DayZ's Enfusion/Arma engine lineage as no Deck-specific guides were found.

KnownIssues: VAC anti-cheat may cause launch issues or bans on some Proton versions — verify the correct Proton build before playing on official servers
Controller/gamepad support is not officially listed; keyboard and mouse bindings may need remapping via Steam Input
Online-only game — no offline play possible, and server browser UI can be difficult to navigate with controller
Some players report stuttering in dense forests or towns due to CPU-bound streaming on the Zen 2 chip

MaxPerformance.Notes: Uncapped at 15 W with full GPU clock, DayZ can approach 60 fps in open terrain but will dip to 40-45 fps in towns or dense forests — consider dropping the cap to 45 if stutters appear. Battery life will be short, so this profile suits docked or plugged-in play.
